title: Ito call stream
description: The JSON text frames on `GET /v0/calls/{call}/stream`. Audio travels in binary frames: 16 kHz 16-bit PCM up, 24 kHz 16-bit PCM down. Both sides ignore frame types they don't recognise.

FromApp.description: A text frame the app sends.

FromServer.description: A text frame the server sends.

CallState.description: `listening` for you; `hearing` the moment your voice is heard, before any words; `turn_ended` once your turn is over (the chime); `working` while Ari works (the tone in silent gaps); `speaking` while Ari's voice plays.

SentenceId.description: Opaque, and unique within the call.

Mute.title: mute
Mute.description: Mutes your microphone: a turn you're in the middle of ends at once, as said so far, and Ari answers it. You can stop sending audio.

End.title: end
End.description: Ends the call, as `POST /v0/calls/{call}/end` does. A turn in progress is sent as it stands.

Played.title: played
Played.description: A sentence's audio has finished playing, or `stop_playback` dropped it. It times when Ari went quiet.

State.title: state
State.description: What the call is doing now. Sent on every change, and first on every connection.

Heard.title: heard
Heard.description: What you're saying, for captions: live while you speak, then `final` with the text as sent and the spoken message's id.

Saying.title: saying
Saying.description: The sentence Ari is about to speak, for captions; its audio follows in the next binary frames. Answer with `played` once it has played.

StopPlayback.title: stop_playback
StopPlayback.description: You spoke over Ari: drop all audio you haven't played, at once, and answer each dropped sentence with `played`.

Problem.title: problem
Problem.description: The call can't go on. The server closes the socket, and the call ends with this reason.
